selected.title: Below the dark mark
selected.texas_link: Texas State University in San Marcos is developing paired pavement imagery for Texas road maintenance.

movement.object: paired surface and depth pavement assessment

selected.why_today: Freshly fetched ongoing phase-two application; last Docket verification September29. No new October2 event or statewide adoption proof. Present as an application explainer if editorial freshness permits.
selected.consequence: Road maintenance engineers receive an assessment report rather than evidence that a road has already been repaired.
selected.application_change: Pairing surface images with depth information helps distinguish stains from road damage for maintenance assessment.
selected.counter_image: The dark stain remains flat while the illustrated crack has depth, and neither road sample is repaired.
selected.earned_take: Finding damage and fixing pavement are different steps, with no measured repair outcome claimed.

agency.next_step: Improve hairline crack detection, automatic severity scoring and adaptation to different surfaces and climates.
agency.who_can_act: Texas State researchers and transportation engineers develop and evaluate the assessment; no public comment deadline is attached.

filmability.viewer_question: Can a dark line on a road tell you which road needs repair?
filmability.opening_action: Illustrated pavement patch contains a flat dark stain beside a genuine recessed crack; a cross section reveals their difference.
filmability.mechanism: One sourced surface-to-depth relationship: similar dark 2D marks separate when depth becomes visible.
filmability.human_consequence: Pavement engineers receive prioritized repair reports; earlier repairs and savings are stated aims, not measured outcomes.
filmability.source_limit: Phase two, closer to statewide use; no adoption date or proven savings. Illustration must not imitate actual AI software or imply perfect classification.
three_key_images: Cross section: flat stain and recess
Repair-report paper entering maintenance queue; no invented repair already completed

asset_leads.inspection: Actual pixels inspected: cracks across yellow painted stripes on asphalt. Static closeup; no scanner, model, workers or location proof.
asset_leads.rights_basis: Filename credits Charlotte Harrison/Unsplash; no license or original Unsplash page authenticated. Not cleared.
asset_leads.asset_fit: Rejected: generic older image cannot establish phase-two action. Original illustration is stronger.

action_support.pictured_action: Cross section opens below dark pavement marks to expose crack depth while stain remains flat
action_support.scope_fit: One simple explanatory mechanism; director-bound independent code/phone/native proof required; Illustration disclosure

action_support.pictured_action: 2D surface and 3D depth become paired, revealing which dark feature is recessed
action_support.scope_fit: Same single mechanism; no bespoke human rig or authentic interface claim

action_support.pictured_action: A repair-report sheet receives the sourced damage distinction and joins a maintenance queue
action_support.scope_fit: Explanatory report relationship, not claimed actual city decision or completed repair; director must bind and prove

visual_stakes.affected_person: Texas pavement maintenance engineers and road users
visual_stakes.visible_change: Surface view opens into a depth cross section
visual_stakes.consequence: Better assessment supports maintenance scheduling; claimed prevention and savings are prospective
visual_stakes.opening_question: Which dark line needs a repair?
visual_stakes.answer: Paired surface and depth imagery helps separate damage from stains; deployment remains in development
visual_stakes.asset_fit: Original disclosed illustration; inspected generic source photograph rejected

action_proposals.visible_action: An illustrative scan traverses two pavement samples. Conserved flat and notched profiles rise from the stain and crack; associated source-grounded report sheets move into a maintenance tray.
action_proposals.consequence: The surface and depth distinction enters an illustrative report without changing or repairing the pavement sample.
action_proposals.limits: Enlarged original explanatory geometry, not a measured sample, actual road, software interface, exact model classification or completed repair. Report sheets symbolize the published report relationship.
action_proposals.source_basis: Texas State describes paired surface images and depth maps distinguishing damage from stains and producing prioritized repair reports. Improvement of hairline detection and severity scoring is planned.
